newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville cuts Fri shoulder hour prices by $6/MWh.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville cuts Fri shoulder hour prices by $6/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) lowered its prices for firm power for Friday shoulder hours (0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) by another $6.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Thursday.
Sales volumes were not limited during those hours, but BPA continued to refrain from offering power during hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PST.
Friday firm power during shoulder hours was offered at $24.00 per MWh to Northwest buyers and at $25.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) deliveries.
Friday offers for firm power during off-peak hours (0100-0600 and 2300-2400) were unchanged at $12.50 per MWh.
Prices for non-firm power during hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 were also unchanged at $12.50 per MWh for Friday, while hours ending 0600 and 2300 were priced at $20.00 (Northwest) and $21.00 (COB).
BPA also posted Saturday offer prices since Monday is Martin Luther King day, a holiday for many utilities.
The agency will post Sunday through Tuesday prices on Friday, a BPA source said.
Saturday with peak firm power was offered at $25.00 in the Northwest and $26.00 at COB, with a 500 megawatt limit.
BPA also continued to offer displacement power for hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PST at $9.00 per MWh.
